sections.h2: What drives the Killeen housing market
sections.html:
Killeen sits outside the East Gate of Fort Hood, and soldiers and their families create much of the demand for houses and rentals. Military moves, deployments and orders therefore set the timing for many sales.

Anyone holding a permanent change of station order cares most about a firm closing date, and an as-is sale can deliver one. The city's newcomer page for the installation links to local resources, transit and parks, which helps when you are pitching to buyers arriving from elsewhere.

sections.h2: Downtown Killeen and the vacant structure rule
sections.html:
Downtown Killeen runs from Rancier Avenue (FM 439) on the north to Veterans Memorial Boulevard (Business 190) on the south, and it is on the National Register.

Downtown Killeen vacant property rules
TopicDetail
AreaRancier Avenue (FM 439) to Veterans Memorial Boulevard (Business 190)
Historic statusFederal historic register
Vacant structure ordinanceAdopted August 4, 2020 (Ordinance No. 20-032)
Office to callDevelopment Services, 200 E Avenue D, 2nd Floor

If your property is empty and lies in the Historic Overlay District, you must register it and pay an annual fee. Phone Development Services before you list, because buyers will ask whether the registration is current.

Killeen uses a council-manager system, with a mayor and seven council members. Permits and code questions go through city Development Services, and the appraisal side sits with the county. Call before listing if you finished a remodel or a fence, so any open permit is closed out before a buyer's lender asks.

Bell Central Appraisal District sets values for Killeen in Bell County, while the city and other units set rates. You can pay at the district's offices with no fee by check, cash or money order. Its online and phone options go through a vendor that charges fees.

It offers a quarterly installment agreement, a homestead delinquent-tax installment agreement and a tax deferral option. A homestead's assessed value may rise up to 10 percent a year until it matches market value, and that increase is mandatory under the Property Tax Code.

Military households should look closely at the veteran items on this list.

  • Residence homestead
  • Disabled person and age 65 or older, including surviving spouses
  • 100 percent disabled veteran or surviving spouse
  • Surviving spouse of a service member killed in action or of a first responder killed on duty
  • Donated residence of a partially disabled veteran

Applicants need a current driver license or Texas ID, a Social Security letter for disability, and a recent VA award letter for a veteran. No annual renewal is needed, though the chief appraiser may request updated applications. The buyer applies for a fresh exemption after you sell.

sections.h2: Texas tax dates around a Killeen sale
sections.html:
A Killeen closing runs on four dates: the January 1 value and lien date, the October bills, the end-of-year split payments and the February 1 delinquency date.

  • Bell CAD lists a discount deadline of October 31 for entities that offer one.
  • A split bill has halves due at the end of November and in June.
  • The protest deadline is generally May 15.

Individual taxing units may offer discounts, so ask the county for the numbers on your parcel.

sections.h2: Options if you must sell fast in Killeen
sections.html:
Orders or a deployment push many owners to move quickly. Three routes are open.

  • An agent listing suits a house in showing shape and an owner without a deadline.
  • Skipping the agent keeps the commission and leaves buyer management to you.
  • A cash offer takes the house unrepaired and sets the closing date with you, which suits a PCS move, a rental with problem tenants or an inherited house.

If you rent the house out from another duty station, the tenant side has its own court process.

Texas Property Code chapter 24B lets an owner ask the sheriff or constable for removal without a court case. The occupant must have stayed after being told to go, the property must not have been open to the public when they entered, no suit may be pending between you, and the occupant cannot be family or a current or former tenant. A removal later found wrongful can bring a lawsuit against the person who asked for it.

A real tenant is different and needs an eviction suit. Adverse possession is another idea: an open, hostile claim to land, with a ten-year period in the usual case. A vacant Killeen rental invites trouble, so check on it often.

sections.h2: Selling a Killeen rental with a tenant
sections.html:
You can sell with the lease intact or end the tenancy as the lease allows. For unpaid rent Texas requires a written notice to vacate, and the suit is filed in justice court. The tenant is served several days before trial, and either side has only five days to appeal to county court.

Once judgment is final, the writ of possession waits a few days and is then followed by a 24-hour warning. Federal notice rules may add time on some covered properties. A cash buyer may take the house with renters still inside, so you skip the court calendar.

sections.h2: Late filing for a disabled veteran exemption
sections.html: Texas lets a disabled veteran apply late in some cases. If you file after April 30, Bell CAD asks you to submit an application anyway so the office can apply any remedy the law provides once it approves. Gather a recent VA award letter before you call. The donated residence of a partially disabled veteran and the surviving-spouse items are named on the district's list.

The Bell County clerk records deeds for land in the county once a notary has acknowledged the signature, and the title company files at closing.

If the loan is behind, Texas runs the foreclosure outside court: a default letter, a short cure window, a courthouse notice and a first-Tuesday auction. If the owner has died, a will normally goes to probate within a few years of the death, and a small estate affidavit is only for modest estates without much real property. Get legal advice before relying on an affidavit.

sections.h2: Preparing a Killeen house for a deadline sale
sections.html: Gather the deed, a lender payoff letter and your Bell County tax statement first. If you are being reassigned, confirm what the buyer will do about your move-out date and tell them in writing when you can hand over the keys. Ask each buyer for a closing date in the offer. A cash buyer can often shape that date around your orders, while a loan buyer needs time for an appraisal. For a house with a tenant, the lease end is the date to build around.

faqs.a: Between Rancier Avenue (FM 439) and Veterans Memorial Boulevard (Business 190), just outside Fort Hood's East Gate.

faqs.q: Is there a vacant house registration in Killeen?
faqs.a: Yes, for vacant structures inside the Historic Overlay District. A 2020 ordinance requires registration with Planning and Development Services and an annual fee.

faqs.q: Which office handles permits in Killeen?
faqs.a: City Development Services, at 200 E Avenue D, 2nd Floor.

faqs.q: Does Bell CAD offer payment plans?
faqs.a: Yes. It lists a quarterly installment agreement, a homestead delinquent-tax installment agreement and a deferral option. Ask the office which applies.

faqs.q: Can a military household sell quickly in Killeen?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers can set the closing date around orders. A traditional listing takes longer but can bring a higher price for a house in good condition.
